extracted.intended_audience: conference publication chairs (main conferences and standalone events); workshop chairs attached to larger conferences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for publication chairs on preparing and delivering conference/workshop proceedings to the ACL Anthology, including metadata, file formats, timelines, copyright, and ingestion procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register your meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a conference publications chair, you must register your intention to submit your proceedings via a Github issue; include the complete list of volumes to be published and the desired publication date. Workshop chairs attached to a larger conference should register through the main conference publication chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do this as early as possible (ideally well before the submission deadline) so the Anthology team can do a quick sanity check of the metadata. Your proceedings will be due no later than two weeks prior to the negotiated publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide venue identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Each venue (conference or workshop) has a venue identifier; a slugified version of the conference acronym (lowercase ASCII letters and numerals) is used in the Anthology URL and as part of the Anthology ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For existing venues, look up the venue’s existing identifier. New venues must have their identifier confirmed by the Anthology director. Do not include the year or meeting number in the identifier (a common mistake is e.g., ACL2020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full volume title
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply the title of the volume book that will be published (e.g., 'Proceedings of the ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a name consistent with prior years' volumes. The full title should not contain abbreviations except parenthetically (e.g., 'Proceedings of the 2019 Meeting of the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)'). If you have sub‑volumes (long papers, short papers, demos, tutorials), append descriptors after the full volume name. Avoid putting the year as the primary identifier of the volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: New venue information (name and website)
rubrics_metrics.description: If your venue is appearing for the first time, provide the venue name and the venue's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venue name should be the name of the venue (not a particular meeting) and must not include the year or meeting number. Website should ideally be the venue's site (e.g., https://naacl.org) rather than a meeting-specific page. This information is stored in the Anthology database and the venue identifier will be confirmed by the Anthology director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request ISBNs
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to publish or print proceedings, you will need an ISBN; the ACL can provide ISBNs for ACL conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact titles of each volume to be assigned an ISBN and send this information to the ACL Business Manager (Jennifer Rachford). The guidance places this step before the paper submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit your data (formats and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: After collecting camera-ready papers and attachments, arrange them into either ACLPUB format (legacy/Softconf) or aclpub2 format, and share them as directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group each volume's directory inside a single top-level folder if submitting multiple volumes. Post a link to this directory on the ingestion request Github issue or share with the Anthology Director via email. Share via HTTP or FTP (preferred for automated download); Dropbox or Google Drive are also acceptable. This sharing should be done two weeks prior to your negotiated publication date to allow processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACLPUB vs aclpub2
rubrics_metrics.description: Two supported proceedings generation formats: legacy ACLPUB (commonly used with Softconf) and newer aclpub2 (supports ARR and OpenReview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using Softconf, you will likely produce ACLPUB output as described in the ACLPUB→Anthology documentation. aclpub2 can be run standalone and is designed to work with ARR/OpenReview. Both formats are supported; choose based on your conference management workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run format checker for aclpub2
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are using aclpub2, run the Anthology format checker on each directory prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The format checker will surface errors that should be fixed before sharing the data with the Anthology to reduce ingestion problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred sharing and ingestion workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anthology ingests submitted data by running scripts that convert it into the authoritative format, apply title-case protection, and disambiguate author names; the result becomes a pull request on the Anthology Github repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the pull request is approved and merged to master, the site is rebuilt automatically (twice a day) and made live. Workshop chairs should handle submission steps through their main conference publication chair rather than contacting the Anthology directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: submit data two weeks before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Your proceedings and associated data should be submitted no later than two weeks prior to the negotiated publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives Anthology staff time to process, convert, and create the pull request in the repository so the site can be rebuilt in time for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright transfer forms (collection and naming)
rubrics_metrics.description: If not using the START system, you should collect copyright transfer forms from authors and submit them with the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ACL copyright transfer PDF template (link provided). Forms should be signed by authors and saved using ACL Anthology identifiers as filenames (e.g., copyright-transfers/P11-1001.pdf). Place them into a folder and deliver them in bulk to the Anthology Editor when submitting proceedings. In aclpub2, copyrights should be listed as paper attachments with a type of 'copyright'. While it is good practice to obtain transfers, the Anthology will ingest materials even if transfers are not on file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming convention and folder organization for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize files into directories per volume and use clear folder naming and file naming conventions (e.g., a folder copyright-transfers/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency with Anthology identifiers and directory structure helps automated ingestion. Group multiple volume directories under a single top-level folder for sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errata and corrections policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication, authors may request errata or revised versions of papers or supplemental attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections after publication can only be applied to individual papers; full proceedings volumes will not be replaced or revised. Refer requesters to the Anthology documentation on errata/corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop chairs must coordinate via main conference chair
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairs of workshops attached to a larger conference should not work directly with the Anthology but instead coordinate through the main conference publication chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many registration and submission steps, including creating the Github ingestion issue and grouping volumes, should be handled by the main conference publication chair for satellite workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid including year or meeting number in identifiers or venue names
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include the year or meeting number in the venue identifier or the venue name submitted to the Anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifiers represent the venue (e.g., ACL) not a specific meeting. Including the year confuses 'meeting' vs 'venue'. Use a slugified acronym without year (e.g., 'acl', not 'acl2020').

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology will assist with questions and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anthology team is willing to accept older proceedings/journals from vetted venues and to help resolve questions about submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For nonstandard situations, file a Github issue or contact the Anthology director directly; include the requested metadata so the team can advise and assist.
